notes: vals.ai is an Astro site and makes no XHR/fetch calls for leaderboard data: every benchmark page is server-rendered with its complete data payload embedded in the props attribute of an <astro-island> element. raw.json stores that payload per benchmark, keyed by URL slug, with Astro's [typeCode, value] prop wrapping undone. No value was altered.

Payload shape per benchmark: {default: {metadata, tasks}}, where tasks maps task key -> model id -> {accuracy, latency, stderr, cost_per_test, temperature, top_p, max_output_tokens, reasoning, reasoning_effort, verbosity, compute_effort, provider, harness}. normalized.json uses the 'overall' task only; all per-subtask breakdowns stay in raw.json.
cost_usd is the site's cost_per_test value (USD for a single test case), not a total run cost. latency_s is the site's latency value in seconds. Both are omitted when the site leaves them null.
rank is computed here by sorting the site's own overall accuracy values descending; it matches the ordering the site displays.
context_window is not published anywhere on vals.ai, so that field is absent from every record.

Models are identified by the provider-qualified id the payload uses (e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-5). Display names are resolved client-side from a JS bundle and are not in the payload, so ids are kept verbatim rather than guessed.

rsi_index is the one exception: a narrative report with five per-task result tables (3 models each) and no published overall score. Those tables were scraped from rendered HTML and appear in normalized.json with a 'task' field and metric 'index_score'; no aggregate was invented. Its date was reformatted from the page's 8/12/2026 to ISO.

Method: the browser (chrome-devtools MCP, isolated context 'vals-ai-20260903') was used to confirm each benchmark page still embeds an astro-island payload with the same [typeCode, value] wrapping, and was used directly to scrape rsi_index's rendered HTML tables (its five task panels are display:none until selected, so extraction read .textContent/DOM structure, not .innerText). The bulk fetch of the other 42 JSON-payload benchmarks was then issued from Node with identical request headers, to avoid a co-resident agent stealing the shared browser's selected-page context mid-script, same as 20260902.
changes_vs_20260902: Pages now render multiple <astro-island> elements whose props contain a 'benchmarkView' key: a small summary-card island plus the full-data island shaped benchmarkView.default -> {metadata, tasks}. The 20260902 scrape apparently didn't hit this ambiguity, but today's first extraction pass grabbed the small summary island by mistake (only the 'overall' task, missing stderr/temperature/etc.), and had to be corrected to explicitly select the benchmarkView.default-shaped island. Final raw.json for this run has been verified to include the full per-model field set (accuracy, latency, stderr, cost_per_test, temperature, top_p, max_output_tokens, reasoning, reasoning_effort, verbosity, compute_effort, provider, harness) and full subtask breakdowns (e.g. corp_fin_v2 still has exact_pages/max_fitting_context/shared_max_context), matching 20260902's shape.

Web Search Index's internal metadata.slug changed from 'web_search' to 'web_search_backends' (the page URL is still /benchmarks/web_search). benchmark_slug in normalized.json reflects this new value; source_url is unaffected. No other slug, benchmark name, or record-count changes were observed: total row_count is unchanged at 2750, and every benchmark_slug except this one has an identical record count to 20260902.
RSI Index's underlying data is unchanged since 20260902 (page still shows 'UPDATED 8/12/2026' and the five task tables have identical model/result/score/cost values).
